title: Predict, verify, then decide
lede: Module M4 estimates where disease risk is rising. QUERRA sends someone to check, records what they find, and a person confirms it. Only confirmed hotspots reach a spray decision. The observations then flow back to help validate M4.
modelNote: This shows the planned behaviour, not measurements. Sprint 3 will measure it, as Annex 1.1 §3.7 requires.

nodes.title: M4 risk and crop-stage outputs
nodes.statusLabel: Provided by Nostradamus · access confirmed in Sprint 1
nodes.text: M4 combines Sentinel-2, ERA5, SoilGrids, IoT and in-situ observations into an estimated cereal growth stage and daily, georeferenced disease-risk layers at 10 m (Annex 1.1 §2.8). QUERRA consumes these outputs. It does not re-implement or redistribute M4's proprietary models.
nodes.interface: Nostradamus Data Cube (dc.load in Cube-in-a-Box) · STAC catalogue

runs.edge: Cached copy on the field unit, synced before leaving
runs.mixed: Cloud (Tier B); compact copy cached on the field unit

nodes.title: Plan a targeted scouting round
nodes.text: Stations near rising risk come first. Fixed stations are kept for comparability, and some low-risk control stations are always visited, so the check does not just confirm the forecast.
nodes.interface: Tier C web view for the advisor

runs.mixed: Advisor view (Tier C), pushed to the field unit

nodes.title: Capture and infer at the station
nodes.statusLabel: Partly in place: capture and GPU inference run on the prototype
nodes.text: Photos are taken with station, visit and specimen IDs, camera settings, and GPS and time where available. Inference runs on the device and shows its uncertainty. Low-confidence or out-of-scope results are routed to review, never shown as a diagnosis.
nodes.interface: Field unit (Tier A) · records published to the IoT Observatory over MQTT

runs.edge: Capture and inference on the field unit (Tier A)
runs.mixed: Capture and inference on the field unit (Tier A)
runs.cloud: Capture on the device; inference only after upload (Tier B)

nodes.title: Independent expert review
nodes.text: A reviewer who did not take the photo confirms, rejects or marks the result unsure. Disagreements with the model are kept. This is the step that turns a forecast into a verified hotspot.
nodes.interface: Review queue (Tier C) backed by the cloud store (Tier B)

runs.mixed: Review queue (Tier C) in the cloud
runs.cloud: Review queue (Tier C) in the cloud

nodes.title: The farmer or advisor decides
nodes.text: Treatment decisions consider only confirmed hotspots, alongside the M4 risk and the advisor's judgement. The product, dose, date and treated area are recorded, which is what a pesticide-use comparison needs.
nodes.interface: Intervention record linked to stations and visits

runs.mixed: Recorded on the field unit or in the advisor view

nodes.title: Feed back to M4 and the Data Cube
nodes.text: Observed growth stages and confirmed or rejected hotspots are returned as documented, FAIR in-situ data, using AGROVOC terms and EPPO codes, so M4's stage and risk estimates can be checked against the field.
nodes.interface: GeoJSON / CSV export · Data Dictionary entry · REST API

kpi.title: Why this matters for the pesticide KPI
kpi.text: Because the forecast, the field check, the decision and the treated area are all recorded, decisions guided by the loop can be compared with standard practice on paired plots. That design must be agreed with the site partner in Sprint 2. No reduction is claimed today.
